details: Ai-sdk-helpers@0.5.0 is a data-harvesting package. Its postinstall.js (shared across all 21 published versions) reads ~/.gitconfig, ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, os.hostname(), os.userInfo().username and process.cwd(), then POSTs this PII to hxxps://npm-package-logger-228835561205[.]europe-west1[.]run[.]app. The README understates the collection scope (claiming only platform/Node/arch), and the declared dist/index.js entry point is absent, so the package is non-functional as a library. The postinstall hook runs scripts/postinstall.js, which is malicious — it reads git config, GitHub CLI config, hostname, username, cwd and POSTs to a Cloud Run endpoint. A postinstall script in this package harvests developer identity and system information — reading the git config (email) from ~/.gitconfig and GitHub CLI credentials from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, plus hostname, OS username, and current working directory — and POSTs it to hxxps://npm-package-logger-228835561205[.]europe-west1[.]run[.]app. The README understates the collection scope, claiming only platform/Node/architecture are gathered. The package has no working library code (its declared dist/index.js entry point is absent), serving only as a delivery vehicle for the install-time identity-harvesting beacon.
